text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Seven opposition parties have formed a pact to field one presidential candidate in elections to be held later this year.
The parties, however, said they would boycott the elections unless government reversed controversial new laws that ban some candidates from standing.
- Magistrates in the mining town on Kitwe went on strike on Thursday to push for better conditions of service.
- The Mineworkers Union of Zambia has demanded that miners be paid their pension contributions before Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) is privatised.
- Japan is closely watching Zambia's electoral process which it considers crucial to Zambia's future development, Japanese ambassador Tadashi Matsui said on Wednesday.
